headline: High-risk data leakage and compliance mismatch: kotaemon’s broad egress and API-key handling can expose sensitive support data, while the pair lacks shared-channel evidence for injection.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-python and kotaemon. A has no runnable surface or I/O, and B’s web UI/files do not imply it ingests A’s outputs by default. Without a bridge, prompt injection is provably blocked.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF A becomes runnable and emits content that B parses as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe A’s outputs into B’s prompt context.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and has broad network egress, so sensitive support data can leave the environment. awesome-python is non-runnable and has no data surfaces, so it does not add protection or containment. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF kotaemon is configured with external API providers, sensitive documents can be transmitted off-host.
IF support transcripts or API keys are loaded into kotaemon, they may be included in outbound requests.
mitigations: Restrict kotaemon to local-only models.
Remove API keys from the runtime unless strictly needed.
Store sensitive documents outside ./ktem_app_data.
Review outbound destinations before enabling ingestion.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress allowlisting.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write or network capability and is not runnable, while kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes under ./ktem_app_data. There is no documented shared mutable resource, so direct write conflict is not established. Uncertainty is low because A contributes no competing capability.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file contention becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator shares git state or a workspace between them, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid sharing git working trees.
Run only one kotaemon instance per workspace.
requires-engineering: add file locks for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a customer-support RAG system that can act on retrieved documents and citations, so if it consumes A-derived content, it may treat that content as authoritative. awesome-python is only a collection and cannot verify or correct downstream actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so severity stays medium.
conditions: IF A-derived text is inserted into kotaemon’s knowledge base, B may surface it as trusted support content.
IF operators rely on kotaemon outputs without human review, incorrect actions can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated answers.
Label imported content with source provenance.
Exclude A-derived content from the support corpus.
requires-engineering: add citation validation checks.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and can send them to external APIs, creating retention and residency concerns. awesome-python is non-runnable and touches no data classes, so it is not the compliance driver. The mismatch is about B’s handling of sensitive support data, with A contributing no offsetting controls.
conditions: IF EU personal data is ingested into kotaemon and routed to a non-EU provider, residency risk exists.
IF retention settings differ between local files and upstream APIs, deletion requests may not fully propagate.
mitigations: Confirm data residency for each configured provider.
Disable external APIs for regulated data.
Set explicit retention limits in kotaemon.
Document deletion/export handling for support transcripts.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
